question: A communications lead inherits a Claude-written fact sheet from a colleague who has left, with no record of what it was based on. What should she do first?
options: A) Publish the fact sheet with a note explaining that its original sources could not be traced by the team.
B) Compare the fact sheet against a second Claude draft written from the same brief and topic.
C) Paste the fact sheet into Claude and ask it to identify which of the statements were made up.
D) Re-establish which sources the fact sheet rests on, since checking needs something to check against.
correct_answers: D) Re-establish which sources the fact sheet rests on, since checking needs something to check against.
explanations: Incorrect. A disclaimer does not make unverified statements safe to publish; it just moves the risk onto the reader.
Incorrect. Agreement between two generated drafts is not evidence, since both can be wrong in the same way.
Incorrect. Claude cannot inspect how an earlier response was produced, and it has no access to the sources that were or were not used.
Correct. Verification is a comparison, and without an agreed set of authoritative sources there is nothing to compare the statements with.
